conviction_note: My four findings net to -2.0 points; I round the forecast to -3.0 because the two bearish items bear directly on tonight's revenue line while the two positive ones bear on the cash line, which moves this stock less, and because the name's own recorded reactions are left-skewed (median absolute reaction 11.6%, only 1 of 7 recorded up) - but the edge here is a revenue-quality tilt, not a call, and I have deliberately not smuggled the base rate into the size.

findings.finding: Champions' FY2026 'record revenue' was entirely one customer: the same significant customer went from 13% of revenue in FY2025 to 24% in FY2026 (13% x $56.9m = $7.4m to 24% x $59.4m = $14.3m, i.e. +$6.9m) while total revenue rose only $2.5m - so every other customer combined shrank from ~$49.5m to ~$45.1m, about -8.8% - and that one customer is also 25% of the year-end receivable.
findings.why_not_priced: The concentration disclosure exists only as a 10-K note (Significant Customers, R13); it is not in the 8-K exhibit 99.1 press release, which carries the income statement and balance sheet but no concentration table, and the word never comes up in the Q4 call, where the framing was '12% growth in TOS services ... without material additions to headcount' i.e. operating leverage. There is no published EPS consensus on this name and no sell-side model, so nobody has rebuilt the revenue bridge. If it were priced you would see the question asked in the Q4 Q&A and you would not see the stock still carrying a 'record year' narrative in every secondary write-up; you would also expect a wider discount than the -8.75% the July 27 print produced off a headline beat.
findings.independence: Same direction from a different line of the same 10-K/press release: deferred revenue fell 43% from $15.443m to $8.828m (a multi-year low) and management attributed the FY26 operating cash drain to 'lower upfront billings' - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/771856/000162828026017345/csbr-20260131.htm (2026-03-12). NOTE: that deferred-revenue figure IS printed in the July 27 press-release balance sheet, so it is more priced than the concentration note, and I have not filed it as a separate finding precisely to avoid counting one revenue-quality story twice.

findings.finding: On June 5, 2026 - inside the quarter being reported tonight - Champions amended its Rockville, MD office/lab lease to run through March 31, 2037, adding roughly $6.3m of ROU asset and lease liability and about $16.9m of undiscounted minimum payments; the company's entire pre-existing lease book was $3.7m of ROU asset and ~$8.0m of minimum payments, against $4.87m of cash and $4.07m of total stockholders' equity.
findings.why_not_priced: It appears in exactly one place: the 10-K subsequent-events note. It is absent from the July 27 press release (whose balance sheet is dated April 30, 2026 and therefore pre-dates it), absent from the earnings call transcript, and there is no 8-K and no press coverage of the lease at all. Tonight is the first time the numbers land on a reported balance sheet - lease liabilities roughly triple and total liabilities rise on the order of a quarter - for a company whose entire equity is $4.1m. If the market had focused on it there would be commentary tying the 11-year commitment to the radiopharmaceutical build-out, and the stock would not be flat-to-up over 20 days.
findings.independence: Consistent with, but from a different source than, the company's continued facility/capability spend: the Aug 31, 2026 announcement of in-house SPECT/CT radiopharmaceutical imaging - https://press.championsoncology.com/champions-oncology-expands-integrated-radiopharmaceutical-development-platform-with-in-house-spect-ct-imaging. That release is the growth-side reading of the same commitment, which is why my band crosses zero.

findings.finding: The 'cash halved to $4.9m' fear that dominated the July 27 reaction is likely to be relieved rather than confirmed tonight: fiscal Q1 is Champions' collection quarter - operating cash flow was +$600k in Q1 FY2026 and +$311k in Q1 FY2025, with cash rising from $9.785m to $10.325m in the year-ago Q1 as receivables fell $1.7m - and the company enters this Q1 with its largest-ever year-end receivable, $13.178m, up $1.97m year over year.
findings.why_not_priced: This requires joining two documents nobody joins on a $49k-a-day name: the FY26 10-K balance sheet (AR $13.178m, cash $4.872m) and the prior-year Q1 10-Q cash-flow statement (Q1 is seasonally cash-generative). Every piece of secondary coverage of the July print stopped at 'ended the year with $4.9 million in cash and no debt' and extrapolated the FY26 burn of $4.5m linearly. If the seasonality were priced there would be no runway framing in the post-print write-ups, and the 10-K's own 'adequate to fund operations through at least August 2027' language would be quoted rather than the cash figure.
findings.independence: Different source, same direction: the FY26 balance sheet also shows accounts payable stretched to $6.903m from $4.248m - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/771856/000162828026049834/R3.htm (2026-07-27). That cuts both ways honestly: it means the AP lever is spent, but it also means the April 30 cash figure was not flattered by it running the other way.

findings.finding: Charles River, whose DSA segment is the closest listed read on preclinical oncology outsourcing demand, said on August 5, 2026 - nine days after Champions last spoke - that it recorded 'the highest net book-to-bill in nearly four years' with improvement 'broad based across our global biopharmaceutical and small and mid-sized biotechnology clients', and raised 2026 organic revenue guidance from -1.5%/-0.5% to 0.0%/+1.0%; that bookings window is precisely Champions' May-July 2026 quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: CRL's own print was covered everywhere and moved CRL; the read-across to a 13.9m-share, 9,450-share-a-day microcap with no analyst coverage is aggregated nowhere. CSBR did not move on August 5. The specific mechanism - Champions' deferred revenue is upfront billings on new bookings, so a bookings recovery in the May-July window would show as a deferred-revenue rebound off the $8.828m multi-year low on tonight's balance sheet - has not been written anywhere I can find. If it were priced you would expect the 20-day run-up to be more than +5.2% on essentially no volume.
findings.independence: none - I could not find a second CRO or a Champions-specific bookings datum covering the May-July 2026 window, and this is a read-across from a differently-mixed business (CRL's strength is regulated safety assessment, which is later-stage than Champions' TOS discovery work), which is why I have sized it small.

Insider activity: no Form 4 since 2026-01-30 and no Form 3/4/5 or SC 13D/G since, despite the stock sitting 37% below its 52-week high - no insider buying to read as a signal, and no selling either

Corellia AI external funding or licensing deal - management said on the Q4 call that 'discussions are active, the feedback is positive' but there is no announcement, no 8-K, and no press release; the only trace is a $129k noncontrolling interest newly on the FY26 balance sheet
Press or trade coverage of the June 5 2026 Rockville lease amendment - none exists outside the 10-K footnote

DEF 14A (2026-08-28): no reverse split, no authorised-share increase, no auditor change, no new related-party transaction beyond $0 of consulting fees to Dr Sidransky in FY26; the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan share reserve is not a print driver

Job-posting counts at the Rockville and Hackensack sites - aggregator listings are undated and the counts differ by two-to-one across ZipRecruiter, Indeed and LinkedIn, so I could not establish a dated trend and dropped the angle rather than cite an undated number
Option chain: baseline reports it unusable (no two-sided ATM legs, 364 total open interest), so there is no implied move and no skew to test a finding against
baseline_tension: There is no skew and no implied move to agree or disagree with, and the +5.2% 20-day run-up is meaningless on 9,450 shares a day; my bearish pair cuts against that drift and against the 'record year' framing the July print left behind, while my positive pair cuts against the baseline's own left-skewed reaction history - which is the honest state of this name, and note that anything found here is essentially untradeable at $49k of daily turnover.
